findings.one_line: For an all-treated (or all-control) pair in the five-type prior, the two observed outcomes have probabilities (1-theta)/2,(1+theta)/2, so its theta-information is 1/(1-theta^2), not (1-r)/((1-r)^2-theta^2); replace the asserted equality and rederive the conservative information bound.

The all-treated/control two-parameter cells have information [1-(theta+phi)^2]^{-1}[[1,1],[1,1]] and [1-(phi-theta)^2]^{-1}[[1,-1],[-1,1]], not the displayed factors (1-r)/((1-r)^2-...); the claimed limiting matrix is not the actual information matrix, so the van-Trees route must be repaired (it may be retained only as a proved Loewner upper bound).

cited_checks.note: The attested Theorem 3.4 gives minimax equality for compact convex spaces and u.s.c.-l.s.c. quasi-concave-convex functions; the node's convex/concave conditions imply these, and compact semicontinuity yields attainment.

The attested Gill--Levit multivariate van-Trees bound supports the scalar-functional information-matrix specialization; the node states the score-identity/pseudoinverse extension explicitly, and the consuming proofs instantiate finite-alphabet differentiability and zero-boundary hypotheses.

The attested source states independent random assignment is minimax and supplies a vertex-restricted least-favourable-prior saddle; this matches the bounded-interval endpoint invocation, with the binary transfer supplied by the proposition's sandwich.
